new_statements.quote: Stress: Stress is not a primary phoneme, although we may recognize different degrees of stress. It is something related to the intonation, and may perhaps be considered as a feature of intonation. There is not a consistent record on stress in my material, and for the time being we shall not be concerned about it.
new_statements.citation: Li, Fang-Kuei (1957). The Jui dialect of Poai: phonology. BIHP: Academia Sinica Series A 28. pp. 551-566.
new_statements.locator: p. 562 (paragraph headed 'Stress:', after the tone distribution and before 'An alternate analysis'); tones p. 561 ('There are six tone phonemes'); juncture/onset of stress p. 554; less-stressed vowel-initial syllables p. 555. File: scan pages 12, 11, 4, 5).
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Re-opened the mirror copy (16 pp., 6.76 MB, scan, no text). Rendered pp. 1-16 in one slotted page render call (150 dpi) and read scan pages 1, 4, 11, 12 as images; then ran ONE slotted tesseract (eng) over the 16 renders (no other scanned running) and saved the page-marked scanned as in the mirror; renders deleted. Title page (scan p.1 = printed p.551): 'THE JUI DIALECT OF POAI: PHONOLOGY / FANG-KUEI LI 李方桂', first sentence 'The Jui dialect spoken in Poai 剝隘 in the district of Funing 富寧, Yunnan, belongs to the Northern group of Tai dialects..' -> same work as the citation (BIHP 28: 551-566; printed page numbers visible). The quoted 'Stress:' paragraph is on printed p.562 (scan p.12) exactly…
new_statements.relation_note: new: nothing on record (guib1244 has no catalog record and no stress statement held by the project; all four sources read earlier were silent). First statement for the language: tonal, stress non-phonemic and treated as intonational, no word-stress rule stated.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Po-ai Jui (Bo'ai, Funing) is a six-tone language (six tone phonemes on sonorant-final syllables, three on checked syllables); Li states that stress is NOT a primary phoneme: degrees of stress exist but stress is 'related to the intonation' and 'may perhaps be considered as a feature of intonation'; no word-stress placement rule is given and he explicitly sets stress aside. Supporting remarks: syllable juncture is marked phonetically by 'the onset of stress' (p. 554); vowel-initial syllables 'are usually less stressed' and never utterance-initial (p. 555); utterance-final particles are toneless and carry intonational pitch (p. 561).
new_statements.exceptions: Vowel-initial syllables (e.g. e: 'one' in mi: hon e: 'once upon a time') 'never occur after a pause or begin an utterance, and are usually less stressed'; when uttered initially or 'in a stressed position' a glottal stop appears (p. 555). Toneless particles at utterance end carry intonation pitch (p. 561). 'There is not a consistent record on stress in my material' (p. 562).
new_statements.identity_note: Li 1957 describes the Jui (Dioi/Buyi-type Northern Tai) dialect of Po-ai 剝隘 (Bo'ai), Funing 富寧 County, Yunnan, from one speaker recorded in 1930 -- the variety Glottolog files under Guibian (Yei) Zhuang guib1244 and that the bibliography's Nong 2020 / Luo 2024 papers revisit. Johnson's two SIL reports concern the Central Taic Nong, Dai and Min Zhuang of Wenshan Prefecture, with Yei Zhuang only as a neighbouring Northern Taic group.
